mechanism: Implements MHSampler for drawing from unnormalized target densities via Random Walk / Independent MH with burn-in, thinning, and acceptance-rate diagnostics; examples are synthetic N(0,1), bivariate normal, Gamma, Beta—no market-state sensor.
data_needed: LogPDF / PropRND / LogPropPDF implementations; start vector; nsamples, burnin, thin
why_new_for_mis: After full read: Bayesian sampling infrastructure and toy-distribution demos only; no regime/vol/liquidity sensing.
quote: The Metropolis-Hastings algorithm is a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method that allows samples to be generated from complex distributions for which direct sampling is not possible.

mechanism: Adaptive MCMC (stepping-out/shrinkage slice sampling) samples posteriors of Bayesian linear and logistic regression on synthetic data; compares posterior means/credible intervals to OLS/IRLS—no live market sensing.
data_needed: Unnormalized log posterior; width, burnin, thin; feature matrix X and responses y
why_new_for_mis: After full read: MCMC black-box for posterior inference on toy models, not a market sensor.
quote: Essentially, the user only needs to be able to encode the target posterior density.

idea_name: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo with mass-matrix adaptation
mechanism: Gradient-based HMC with leapfrog integration, MAP warm-start (L-BFGS), EMA epsilon adaptation, Hessian/iterative mass-matrix tuning, and R-hat/ESS/MCSE diagnostics; stress-tested on a 100-D correlated heteroscedastic normal—Bayesian tooling, not market sensing.
data_needed: LogTarget + GradLogTarget; chain count; leapfrog L; target accept; optional mass tuning
why_new_for_mis: After full read: high-dimensional MCMC engine and diagnostics only.
quote: As a stress test to demonstrate the capabilities of HMC, we will consider a 100-dimensional correlated, heteroscedastic normal distribution.

mechanism: V-in-V three-layer partition with anchored expanding PurgedWalkForwardCV: commit config, then score successive non-overlapping Final Test windows; edge that holds in some windows and fails in others is treated as genuine regime sensitivity of the strategy across calendar regimes.
data_needed: Time-ordered X,y,t1; estimator; n_splits; inner_val_pct/final_test_pct; embargo
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic financial ML series; demo RandomForest on 1000 business-day synthetic bars from 2018
why_new_for_mis: Turns multi-window OOS score divergence into an explicit sensor that the edge is regime-conditioned rather than a single pooled Sharpe.
quote: A strategy that performs well in some windows and fails in others is revealing genuine regime sensitivity — a finding a single test window would completely obscure.

mechanism: CombinatorialPurgedCV generates C(N,k) purged/embargoed splits, recombines them into φ[N,k] full-timeline OOS backtest paths, and reports the distribution of path Sharpes; narrow positive path distribution ⇒ temporal robustness, high path variance ⇒ fragile across fold assignments.
data_needed: Event t1 series; features/labels; close prices for MtM Sharpe; n_folds, n_test_folds, pct_embargo
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Financial time series with overlapping labels/features; example N=6,k=2 → 5 paths
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a combinatorial path-robustness sensor that standard single-split CV cannot, conditioned on purge/embargo of temporal leakage.
quote: A strategy with a narrow, positive distribution of path outcomes across all combinatorial fold assignments has demonstrated robustness across many different temporal configurations.

mechanism: Divide history into S even subsets; for every C(S,S/2) symmetric IS/OOS split, take best-IS strategy and record whether its OOS rank is below the median; PBO = fraction of such below-median splits—quantifies selection-process unreliability over a candidate matrix.
data_needed: returns_matrix (T×N strategies); even n_folds (8–16); performance metric (default Sharpe)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any strategy-return panel; demo 50 noise strategies × 500 business days
why_new_for_mis: Single falsifiable probability that MIS can attach to a candidate shortlist as a selection-bias sensor before promoting a strategy.
quote: the proportion of splits where the best in-sample strategy ranked below the median out-of-sample is the PBO estimate.

mechanism: Abstracts HistorySelect/HistoryDealGet* behind ITradeRepository with live and mock implementations so analytics (win rate, DD, equity panel) are unit-testable offline—software architecture, not market sensing.
data_needed: Closed deals via History API or hardcoded STradeRecord array; magic/date filters
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Mock FX symbols EURUSD/GBPUSD/USDJPY/AUDUSD/USDCAD; live account history lookback days
why_new_for_mis: After full read: DIP/testability plumbing only.
quote: The repository pattern resolves these issues by making data dependencies explicit and injectable via an ITradeRepository* pointer.

idea_name: Drawdown DNA: Ulcer, Pain, time-underwater episode sensor
mechanism: Rebuild equity and underwater curve from daily closed PnL; split into peak→trough→recovery episodes; compute Ulcer Index (RMS of daily underwater %), Pain Index (mean underwater %), time-underwater %, Recovery Factor; weighted resilience grade; slow-bleed high time-underwater/Ulcer flagged as possible edge decay in current regime.
data_needed: CSV Date,DailyPnL; start capital; min episode depth %; score weights
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any strategy daily closed-PnL series (backtest or account); durations in trading-day records
why_new_for_mis: Moves beyond single max-DD to a persistence/depth DNA that can sense when an edge’s equity path is chronically underwater (regime-decay symptom).
quote: a curve that is rarely deep but almost always underwater is often a sign of an edge that has decayed.

mechanism: On closing-deal PnL: Gini of winners, top-N share of net/gross, concentration profile (top 1/5/10/25/50% winners), one-sided stress removing best K% winners (survival ratio), and largest calendar-day share vs prop consistency limit; composite concentration grade.
data_needed: CSV Date,Profit per closing deal; TopN; RemovePct; consistency limit %
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any closed-trade list (≥20, preferably 100+); deal-level not full-position PnL
why_new_for_mis: Senses whether reported edge is broad or rests on a few outlier trades/days—fragility feature MIS can gate before trusting a strategy stream.
quote: if the best few trades had not happened, would the strategy still be profitable?

mechanism: Reconstruct closed positions from account deals, attribute by magic or normalized comment, map net PnL onto a daily calendar grid per strategy, compute pairwise Pearson r of daily returns over the selected date range, and render a symmetric correlation heatmap to flag nominal vs genuine diversification.
data_needed: Account deal history (HistorySelect); magic/comment filters; dateFrom/dateTo; ≥2 active strategies
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Multi-EA account portfolio; daily aggregation of closed-position returns; example snapshot 94 positions
why_new_for_mis: Live portfolio sensor of strategy co-movement that detects redundancy/risk concentration hidden by aggregate account metrics.
quote: The correlation matrix identifies these dependencies, allowing developers to see whether diversification is genuine or merely nominal.

idea_name: Walk-Forward Efficiency (WFE) overfit and transfer sensor
mechanism: On per-bar equity returns, roll IS length L_IS then OOS L_OOS; annualized Sharpe per slice; WFE=SR_OOS/SR_IS with guards (SR_IS≤0 or SR_IS<min⇒WFE=0); pass if WFE≥0.5; aggregate mean/std/pass-rate and CCanvas histogram—scores whether calibrated parameters transfer or collapse at IS/OOS boundaries (incl. regime-transition Sharpe compression).
data_needed: CSV per-bar equity returns; L_IS, L_OOS; annualization (D1=252,H4,H1,M15); threshold; min_is_sharpe
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD Daily 2021–2025; L_IS=252, L_OOS=63 → 16 windows; MA crossover demo
why_new_for_mis: Native absolute metric of OOS transfer efficiency that MIS can use to reject curve-fit parameter sets without visual equity inspection.
quote: A value near 1.0 means the parameter set transferred its performance to forward data intact. A value near 0 means the in-sample performance was largely artificial.

idea_name: Execution-cost cushion and thin-winner erosion sensor
mechanism: Model cost = Fixed + CostPerLot×Volume; breakeven cost = avg edge/deal; cushion = net / total assumed cost; reprice all deals across cost multipliers; count winners flipped to losers and gross profit in thin winners (result ≤ ThinMult×their cost); grade cost-robustness—senses how much spread/slippage/commission the edge absorbs.
data_needed: CSV Date,Profit,Volume per closing deal; CostPerLot; CostFixed; cushion target
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any deal stream; sample 200 deals / ~67.9 lots; default 12 units/lot
why_new_for_mis: Quantifies liquidity/execution-friction fragility of an edge (cushion, win erosion) rather than only backtest net profit.
quote: how much execution cost can a strategy absorb before its edge disappears?

idea_name: Mann-Whitney U trade-return distribution regime comparator
mechanism: Extract volume×tick_value-normalized closing-deal returns in two date windows; rank-pool with tie correction; U/z/p via normal approximation; dual Tukey box plots—rejects identical distributions when one period stochastically dominates, informing whether two market periods warrant different parameter sets.
data_needed: History deals DEAL_ENTRY_OUT for one symbol; two datetime windows; α; preferably ≥20 trades/group
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Chart symbol (e.g. AUDJPY H1 demo); user-defined half-year windows (e.g. 2024 H1 vs H2)
why_new_for_mis: Distribution-free sensor that two calendar regimes produce different trade-return laws, avoiding mean/t-test fragility to fat-tail outliers.
quote: For a trader deciding whether two market regimes warrant different parameter sets, this is the more relevant question.

mechanism: Reconstructs IN/OUT deals into CTradeRecord, draws entry/exit/SL/TP chart objects, and arrow-key steps through trades with viewport centering—qualitative review UI, no automatic market sensor.
data_needed: Closed deal history; symbol/magic/date filters; chart focus for keys
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: User symbol/TF (example EURUSD M15); any reconstructed closed trades
why_new_for_mis: After full read: manual visualization/navigation tool only.
quote: Neither shows the chart context at entry. Neither shows how price behaved during the holding period.
